Problem Statement 44 45 ### 1.1 Context 46 47 Zimmermann's storefront runs on SFCC B2C Commerce with a PWA Kit front end hosted on Managed Runtime (MRT). Editorial and CMS content (banners, homepage modules, navigation, footer, size guides, editorial blocks) is owned by Contentful and managed by the Zimmermann content team; commerce data (products, pricing, inventory, orders) is owned by SFCC. A dedicated Contentful squad will own the full Contentful setup under a separate statement of work; the Accenture squad must build and document the SFCC-side integration before that squad onboards. 48 49 ### 1.2 Problem 50 51 Editorial content authored in Contentful must render on the correct SFCC storefront pages. Some content is global; some must appear only on a specific category or product page. Contentful holds no knowledge of the SFCC catalogue, and the two systems must remain decoupled. The team needs one defined, correct mechanism for the PWA/MRT layer to decide which Contentful entries render on which SFCC page, cache-safely and consistently across the storefronts, together with a clear account of what the Accenture squad must build on the SFCC side (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration, integration wiring) before the Contentful squad onboards. 52 53 ### 1.3 Impact if Not Solved 54 55 Without a defined pattern the squad risks building inconsistent per-component ID-matching logic, coupling Contentful to the SFCC catalogue, or serving cached editorial content on the wrong category or product pages. The incoming Contentful squad would lack a briefing artefact, and integration blockers (credentials, per-environment configuration, unresolved content ownership) would surface late in the build. 56 57 ### 1.4 Success Criteria 58 59 1. One documented mechanism exists for scoping and rendering Contentful editorial content on the correct SFCC pages, decoupled from the SFCC catalogue. 60 2. The SFCC-side build scope (content types, consuming components, rendering logic, locale configuration) is enumerated and traceable to Jira stories. 61 3. The Accenture versus incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary is defined. 62 4. Blockers and dependencies for the Contentful squad's onboarding are identified with owners. 63 5. The design is cross-checked against the codebase, Jira, and Confluence for accuracy. 64 65 *These criteria map to the validation in Section 6.* 66 67 --- 68 69 ## 2. Constraints & Assumptions 70 71 ### 2.1 Constraints 72 73 | Constraint | Detail | 74 | --- | --- | 75 | Platform | SFCC B2C Commerce + PWA Kit on MRT. No alternative platform is in scope. | 76 | Sole CMS | Contentful is the sole CMS across all storefronts (HPC-001). SFCC does not connect to Contentful directly; all CMS content is fetched by the MRT Node layer, not by SFCC cartridges or Business Manager. | 77 | Contentful environments | A single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias for zero-downtime releases. Decided by Tim Lavelle (see Section 8). | 78 | Schema as code | Content types are Git-managed definitions deployed via CI (`npm run sync:contentful`), not hand-created in the Contentful UI. | 79 | Storefront and locale scope | The solution must work across 8 storefronts and 9 Contentful locales (serving 11 storefront-locale URL routes across 10 PWA sites). No single-market workarounds. See Section 5.5 and the REG-005 risk in Section 7. | 80 | Product data path | Product data reaches SFCC via AP21 through MuleSoft; Contentful editorial is independent of that path and never flows back to SFCC. | 81 82 ### 2.2 Assumptions 83 84 | Assumption | Risk if Wrong | 85 | --- | --- | 86 | Editorial content is fetched browser-direct (client-side) today; SSR-first fetching is the target architecture and is not yet built. | If SSR-first is not adopted, SEO/LCP-critical editorial renders client-side (spinner on first paint) and the SSR cache-key rules in Section 5 do not apply. | 87 | The Contentful "Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app" is installed and lets authors associate SFCC product/category references. | If the connector app's field type and payload shape differ from the assumed ShortText model, the content-model field definitions need revision (owned by SFCC-238). | 88 | US-International (REG-005) is a Confirmed requirement but is not yet in Business Manager or the routing config (`sites.overlay.js`). | If it lands before bootstrap it may add a 10th Contentful locale and change the built SFCC-site count. Tracked in Section 7. | 89 | Sprint-2 content-type field sets are inferred from UI and Jira, not confirmed schema. | If the authoring review (Emma and Dani) changes them, the Sprint-2 definitions must be updated before build. | 90 | The Contentful account is on the Enterprise plan. | If not, the production alias (zero-downtime releases) is unavailable. | 91 92 --- 93 94 ## 3. Options Analysis 95 96 > The core design question this spike was tasked to answer is how Contentful editorial content is scoped to, and rendered on, the correct SFCC pages. Only one genuine options decision exists here. The other architectural choices are settled elsewhere (single Space versus multiple Spaces was decided by Tim Lavelle and is recorded in Section 2 and Section 8) or are current-versus-target build-status gaps (client-side versus SSR-first fetch, covered in Section 5), not options to weigh in this document. 97 98 ### 3.1 Options Summary 99 100 | Option | Pros | Cons | Viable? | 101 | --- | --- | --- | --- | 102 | **A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering** | + Keeps Contentful and SFCC decoupled (no catalogue duplication or sync).
+ SSR-first: editorial content is in the initial HTML (SEO, no content flash).
+ Components stay presentation-only and reusable across ID scopes.
+ The ID is a structural, non-localized field: one value across all locales. | - Authors enter a raw ID with no referential-integrity check against the live catalogue (typo risk).
- SSR cache keys must include the SFCC ID or cached content leaks across pages.
- Filtering logic is centralised in the MRT SSR layer, which must be correct. | Yes (recommended) | 103 | **B - Mirror the SFCC catalogue into Contentful and use reference fields** | + Authors select real products/categories (referential integrity, no typos). | - Requires a sync pipeline from SFCC to Contentful (build, maintain, drift).
- Couples the two systems.
- Disproportionate to current editorial volume. | Considered, not selected | 104 | **C - Filter client-side in the React component** | + Simplest to implement initially. | - Editorial content absent from the SSR HTML (SEO loss, content flash).
- Ships unneeded entries to the browser.
- Puts matching logic in the component, breaking the presentation-only contract. | No | 105 106 > **Honesty note:** the source design documents Option A as the resolved approach; Options B and C are recorded here as the genuine design space, not as alternatives that were formally weighed. The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app is closer to Option B for the authoring step, and its field/payload shape (and therefore whether A's plain-ShortText choice survives) is the subject of SFCC-238. 107 108 ### 3.2 Option Detail 109 110 #### Option A - SFCC ID + MRT SSR-side filtering 111 112 SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain, non-localized ShortText fields (`sfccProductId`, `sfccCategoryId`) on the Contentful content type. At render time the MRT SSR layer fetches all published entries of a content type for the current locale, filters them by matching the ID field against the current page context, and passes only the matched entries to a presentation-only React component. A null ID means "show on all pages of this type". This fits the decoupling and SSR/SEO constraints in Section 2 and is detailed in Section 5. 113 114 #### Option B - Mirror the catalogue into Contentful (not selected) 115 116 Editors would pick real SFCC products/categories via Contentful reference fields backed by a synchronised copy of the catalogue. This removes the typo risk but requires a sync pipeline and couples the two systems; it is disproportionate to the current editorial volume. 117 118 #### Option C - Client-side filtering *(Discarded)* 119 120 Discarded: fetching all entries and filtering in the browser keeps editorial content out of the SSR HTML, which violates the SSR-first / SEO constraint and pushes ID-matching logic into components. 121 122 --- 123 124 ## 4. Recommended Option & Rationale 125 126 ### 4.1 Recommended Option 127 128 **Option A - SFCC ID as a non-localized ShortText field, resolved by MRT SSR-side filtering.** 129 130 ### 4.2 Rationale 131 132 Option A is the only approach that keeps Contentful decoupled from the SFCC catalogue while placing editorial content in the server-rendered HTML (satisfying the SSR/SEO constraint) and keeping components presentation-only. Option B solves the authoring typo risk but pays for it with a sync pipeline and coupling not justified by the current editorial volume; Option C is disqualified by the SSR/SEO constraint. Reference-resolution (turning an ID into rendered commerce data) is out of scope for this document and is owned by SFCC-238. 133 134 ### 4.3 Trade-offs Accepted 135 136 - Authors enter SFCC IDs by hand with no referential-integrity guardrail (typo risk). The installed Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app may improve the authoring step; the field mechanic is confirmed by SFCC-238. 137 - Every SSR cache key for an ID-scoped page must include the SFCC ID; omitting it leaks editorial content across category or product pages. 138 - This is proposed design, not yet implemented. Adopting it also commits to the not-yet-built SSR-first fetch (Section 5). 139 140 --- 141 142 ## 5. Technical Implementation 143 144 ### 5.1 High-Level Sequence (target SSR-first flow) 145 146 1. A shopper requests an SFCC page (for example a PLP for category X). 147 2. The MRT SSR layer fetches all published Contentful entries of the relevant content type for the current locale via the Contentful Delivery API (CDA). 148 3. The SSR layer filters entries by matching the SFCC ID field (`sfccCategoryId` / `sfccProductId`) against the current page context; a null ID means show on all pages of that type. 149 4. The SSR layer passes only the matched, pre-filtered entries to the React component. 150 5. The component renders the entries it receives, in order. If the array is empty it renders nothing (null return, no DOM output). 151 6. The SSR response is cached with a key that includes locale + the SFCC ID (+ page number if paginated). 152 7. On editor publish, Contentful fires an HMAC-signed webhook to the MRT receiver, which purges the affected cache keys. 153 154 > **Current state:** steps 2 to 5 run client-side today (`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, a `useEffect` REST fetch with `include=2` for linked assets). The SSR-first fetch, a GraphQL query layer, and the publish-webhook receiver (step 7) are documented targets and do not exist in the codebase yet. Squads must not assume SSR editorial is live. 155 156 ### 5.2 Component / API Changes 157 158 | File / Endpoint | Change Required | Type | 159 | --- | --- | --- | 160 | MRT SSR layer | Add server-side CDA fetch, SFCC-ID filtering, and cache-key construction (locale + SFCC ID [+ page]). | New | 161 | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` | Replace the client-side `useEffect` fetch with SSR-first data loading; keep client fetch only where SSR is not applicable. | Modified | 162 | `POST /webhooks/contentful` | HMAC-verified cache-purge receiver in the MRT Node layer (verify `X-Contentful-Signature` against `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).
